title: 1-1-prep-lucas-reed-priya-shah
content:
Context: weekly 1:1 with Priya (IC4 backend engineer) — focus on project health for KV-cache improvements, career path discussion, and immediate blockers. Quick wins to unblock spike and get perf numbers for Quarterly Review (Q1).

Agenda (30 minutes):
- 5m quick personal check-in (well-being, workload)
- 10m project status: KV cache refactor (ENG-4231)
  - current perf: +8% p50 latency reduction in branch vs main (local bench)
  - remaining work: integration tests, canary rollout config, benchmark infra scaling
  - ask: estimate for integration + canary (Priya) and risks
- 7m blockers & resourcing
  - flaky integration test causing CI delays (~2-3 runs failing intermittently)
  - Need review + merge on PR 812 (code owner: Marco) — discuss how to get review scheduled
  - dependency on infra change (autoscaler config) scheduled for next week — contingency plan if delayed
- 5m career/checkpoint
  - progress on leadership track: mentoring hours, design reviews, owning a small cross-team project
  - discuss stretch assignment options for H2
- Follow-ups and action items

Notes to self (phrasing for 1:1):
- Start light: "How was your week? Anything non-work urgent?"
- Acknowledge recent wins: "Nice work landing the perf microbench — product team saw promising numbers."
- Signal partnership on flaky tests: "Let's pair briefly on test flakes after this or I can pull in SRE for triage. We should reduce CI churn before canary."
- Be explicit about expectations for canary: timeboxed rollouts, metrics to watch (p50/p95, token throughput, error rates), rollback criteria.

Open questions to surface to Priya:
- Do you feel you have bandwidth to drive the integration tests end-to-end this sprint? If not, what would help (reviewers, SRE time, pairing)?
- Any unknowns in the autoscaler change that could force us to delay canary?
- How comfortable are you leading a short cross-team sync with console & infra next week?

Blockers / Risks (short bullets):
- CI flakes (integration test) -> delays on merge and canary start -> risk to Q1 metric target
- Reviewer availability (Marco overloaded) -> need backup reviewer or manager escalation
- Autoscaler infra change may land after our planned canary window -> need fallback (manual capacity bump on dedicated pool)

Action items (assigned / due):
- Priya: estimate for integration + canary steps (hours + proposed rollout timeline) — due 2026-02-24
- Lucas (me): ping Marco and propose 1hr review slot; if no response by 2026-02-23 escalate to eng lead — due 2026-02-23
- Priya + SRE: triage session for flaky test (30–60m) — schedule by 2026-02-25
- Priya: draft canary runbook with metrics/rollback criteria (doc) — due 2026-02-26; link to include in PR description
- Lucas: prep short note for PM + Console team about canary (impact & monitoring needs) — due 2026-02-25

Career / growth notes (for conversation):
- Positive signals: Priya ran two design reviews this quarter, mentored junior dev on async caching patterns.
- Areas to coach: cross-team communication (owning the sync), stakeholder visibility (weekly status digest).
- Suggestion: Offer Priya a 2-month stretch to own "canary playbook" for serving-runtime — small cross-team leadership exposure; measure success by clean rollout and retro write-up.

Follow-up after 1:1 (post meeting checklist):
- Add action items to Priya's JIRA ticket (ENG-4231) and link canary runbook doc
- Update weekly eng sync slide with perf numbers and planned canary date
- If reviewer remains blocked, assign secondary reviewer (Anika) and update PR 812 reviewers list
- Book 30m pairing session for CI flakes if agreed in 1:1

Random notes / scratch:
- Potential quick mitigation: add integration test to run in parallel on a more stable runner (SRE). Ask Matt in infra.
- If canary delayed >1 week, propose manual traffic shaping by weight on router as contingency (requires Console team support).

Tone reminders: be supportive, focus on removing friction, enable ownership rather than doing tasks for Priya. Call out specific appreciation items.

End of doc.
